Alpina Motors Announces $450 Million Plant Expansion in Turkey as Automotive Sector Grows

Istanbul—Alpina Motors revealed on Tuesday its plans to invest $450 million to expand its manufacturing facility in Bursa, marking a significant commitment to Turkey’s fast-growing automotive sector. The expansion, scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2024, is expected to increase the plant’s annual production capacity by 60,000 units, a 35% rise from current levels.

The investment comes as Turkey consolidates its position as a key automotive production hub, with the sector accounting for nearly 15% of the country’s total exports last year. “This expansion reflects our long-term confidence in Turkey’s skilled workforce and strategic location,” said Alpina Motors CEO Cemal Ergin in a statement. “We look forward to deepening our partnerships with local suppliers and contributing to the region’s economic growth.”

Industry analysts welcomed the announcement, noting that recent currency stabilization and government incentives have renewed international interest in Turkey’s manufacturing landscape. “Automotive firms see Turkey as an efficient gateway to both European and Middle Eastern markets,” said Melis Karadeniz, an analyst at Eurasia Industry Insights. “Alpina’s expansion underscores the resilience of the sector.”

The Turkish Automotive Manufacturers Association estimates that the project could support up to 1,200 new jobs in the region, both directly and through the supply chain. Alpina Motors also indicated that a portion of the investment will be dedicated to improving energy efficiency and adopting advanced manufacturing technologies.

The new production lines are expected to be operational by late 2025, further strengthening Turkey’s role as a regional automotive powerhouse.
